text: Yesterday you were trembling for a health that is dear to you. To day you fear for your own. To morrow it will be anxiety about money the day after, to morrow the diatribe of a slanderer the day after that the misfortune of some friend then the prevailing weather then something that has been broken or lost, then a pleasure with which your conscience and your vertebral column reproach you. Again the course of public affairs.

But there is always a stronger sense of life when the sun is brilliant after rain. And now he is pouring down his beams, and making sparkles among the wet straw, and lighting up every patch of vivid green moss on the red tiles of the cow shed, and turning even the muddy water that is hurrying along the channel to the drain into a mirror for the yellow billed ducks, who are seizing the opportunity of getting a drink, with as much body in it as possible.

But reckoning time, whose millioned accidents, Creep in twixt vows, And change decrees of kings, Tan sacred beauty, blunt the sharpest intense, Divert strong minds to the course of altering things Alas, why fearing of time's tyranny? Might I not then say, Now I love you best, When I was certain o'er in certainty, Crowning the present, doubting of the rest?

warmup.text: As she awaited her guests, she surveyed the table with both satisfaction and disquietude, for her social functions were few. Tonight there were, she checked them off on her fingers, Sir James Crichton, the rich English manufacturer and Lady Crichton, mister and Mrs. Vanderpool, mister Harry Cresswell and his sister, John Taylor and his sister, and mister Charles Smith, whom the evening papers mentioned as likely to be United States Senator from New Jersey a selection of guests that had been determined unknown to the hostess by the meeting of cotton interests earlier in the day.
